title: Bacon or side pork, fresh, cooked

content.title: About
content.content: Bacon or side pork is meat taken from the belly area of a pig. When fresh and cooked, it has a tender texture, a mildly salty aroma, and a soft mouthfeel. It is used in hot dishes, salads, appetizers, and as a garnish for main courses.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional bacon is made from pork belly, but side pork can be prepared in the same way.
Different countries have their own methods: smoking, boiling, or pan‑frying.
Pork is a rich source of high‑quality protein and B‑vitamins, especially B12.
In Russia bacon is often served with potatoes, while in Japan thin slices appear in ramen.
The term “side pork” is sometimes used in culinary schools to refer to slightly leaner cuts than classic bacon.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Bacon provides complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains B1, B2, B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains zinc and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health and blood formation.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb diets such as keto.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bacon is often cured with salt, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: A large amount of saturated fat can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible for individuals allergic to pork meat.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Undercooked bacon may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure it is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bacon can be pan‑fried until crisp, added to soups, stews, salads, or used as a sandwich filling. Cooked slices are also great for cold appetizers when cut thinly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked bacon in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 2 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration – signs of spoilage.
